title: God, Are You Even Listening?! My Meltdown with the Almighty
paragraphs: The big problem God showed Habakkuk, and here's how it went down:

God, how long do I have to yell for help before you actually listen? How many times do I have to be like, "Help! Murder! Someone call the cops!" before you step in and do something? Why do you make me look at all this evil, just staring trouble in the face day after day? It's pure chaos and violence, with fights and arguments breaking out all over. The law is basically falling apart, and justice is a total joke. The wicked have the good people cornered, and they've completely twisted what's right.

And God's like, "Look around at the nations that don't follow me. Look long and hard. Get ready for a shock, because something is about to happen that you'll find hard to believe. I'm about to bring in the Babylonians to punish you. Yeah, the Babylonians—they're fierce and ferocious, a world-conquering force, just grabbing up nations left and right. They're a terrifying people who make up their own rules as they go. Their horses are fast as the wind, and they attack like hungry wolves. A whole stampede of them thunders in from out of nowhere. They come down like vultures circling their prey. They are out to kill; death is what they're all about. They collect victims like a squirrel gathers nuts. They mock kings, laugh at generals, spit on fortified cities, and leave them in the dust. They'll be blown away by the wind. They're so bold in their sin that they think their own strength is their god."

God, you're eternal, right? Holy God, we're not all going to die, are we? God, you chose the Babylonians to carry out your judgment? My Rock, my solid foundation, you gave them the job of disciplining us? But you can't be serious! You can't stand evil! So why aren't you doing something about this? Why are you silent right now? This is an outrage! Evil people are swallowing up the righteous, and you just stand there and watch!

You're treating people like fish in the ocean, swimming around without any direction, not really getting anywhere. Then this evil Babylonian comes along and goes fishing. He pulls in a huge catch. He gets his limit and fills his bucket—a great day of fishing for him! He's so happy! He praises his rod and reel, puts his fishing gear on an altar, and worships it! It's made his day, and he's going to eat well tonight!
Are you just going to let this go on and on? Are you going to let this Babylonian fisherman keep fishing like it's a hobby, killing people as if they're nothing more than fish?

title: God's Response is Coming, Just Wait For It
paragraphs: So, what's God gonna say to all my questions? Honestly, I'm prepping for the worst. I'm gonna go up to my watchtower, scan the horizon, and just wait. I'm waiting to see what God says, how he's gonna answer my complaint.

And then God hit me back: “Write this down. Write what you see. Put it in huge, bold letters so anyone can read it on the fly. This message, this vision, is a preview of what's coming. It’s hyped for its own arrival—it can hardly wait! And it’s no lie. If it seems like it’s taking its sweet time, just wait. It’s on its way. It will show up at the perfect moment.

“Look at that guy, all puffed up with his own ego—so full of himself, but his soul is totally empty. But the person who is right with God because they trust and stick with him? That person is truly alive, like, for real alive.

“And for real, money is a total scam. The arrogant rich people? They never last. They're hungrier for more cash than the grave is for dead bodies. Just like death, they always want more. But the 'more' they collect is just... more death. They're like walking cemeteries of dead nations, graveyards of bodies. Don't even give people like that a second thought. Pretty soon, the whole world will be making fun of them, saying:

“‘Who do you think you are, getting rich by stealing and ripping people off? How long do you think you can get away with it?’ Seriously, how long until the people you’ve crushed wake up, stand up, and make you the one who's getting crushed? You’ve wrecked nation after nation. Now it’s your turn to get a taste of your own medicine. All the survivors are coming to take back what's theirs, as payback for all your violence and killing.

“‘Who do you think you are, grabbing and looting everything, living the high life like you're king of the world, above all the drama and problems? You've basically set up your own downfall. By wrecking others, you've wrecked yourself. You've destroyed your own foundation, and your soul is rotten. The very bricks of your house will call you out, and the woodwork will testify against you.

“‘Who do you think you are, building a city on murder and a town on crime? Don't you get it? The LORD of Heaven’s Armies will make sure all that work just turns to ash. The harder you work at that evil stuff, the less you become. Meanwhile, the whole world is filling up with the knowledge of God's glory, like water covering the sea.

“‘Who do you think you are, getting your neighbors wasted at your parties, pushing drinks on them just to see them naked? You thought you were having the time of your life, but you were wrong. It's your time to be disgraced. While you were busy partying, you were actually drinking from the cup of God's anger. You're going to wake up with a massive hangover—a hangover from the violence in Lebanon, from all the animals you slaughtered, from all the murder and chaos, from violating people and places.

“‘And what's the point of a carved idol, even if it's skillfully made? What good is a fancy metal statue when it just tells you lies? What's the logic in a religious person making a god that can't even speak? Who do you think you are, telling a piece of wood to ‘Wake up,’ or a silent stone to ‘Get up’? Can they teach you anything? They're all surface-level, with nothing on the inside.
“But yo, listen up! God is in his holy Temple! So everyone, be quiet—a holy silence. Just listen.”

title: Habakkuk's Prayer Goes HARD
paragraphs: A prayer from the prophet Habakkuk, orchestra and all:

God, I've heard the stories our ancestors told about you, and I'm literally stopped in my tracks, down on my knees. Please, do the same awesome stuff for us that you did for them. Work your magic for us like you did for them. And yeah, I know judgment is coming, and you have to do it, but please, don't forget to show some mercy.

God is on the move again, taking that same old salvation road trip. He's coming up from the south, from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. The sky is just blazing with how awesome he is, and the whole world is singing his praises. His brightness is like a sunrise cloud, just exploding and spreading out, with forked lightning shooting out of his hand—like, for real, the power in that fist is insane! Sickness marches ahead of him, and plagues follow right behind. He stops, and the Earth just shakes. He looks around, and whole nations are trembling. The mountains that have been around forever just crumble to pieces, and the ancient hills totally collapse like a popped balloon. The paths God walks are older than the oldest mountains and hills. I saw everyone freaking out, totally panicking. Even the old enemies from the wilderness, Cushan and Midian, were terrified, hoping he wouldn't even look their way.

God, are you mad at the River? Are you angry at the good old River? Were you ticked off at the Sea when you rode your horse and chariot to save everyone? You pulled out your bow and just let a whole bunch of arrows fly. You split the Earth open with rivers. The mountains saw it coming and were twisting in pain. Flood waters just poured in. The ocean roared and made these huge waves. The sun and moon just stopped where they were. Your flashing arrows made them stop, and your lightning-strike spears totally nailed them. You were so angry, you stomped all over the Earth. You were furious, and you crushed the godless nations. You were out there to save your people, to save the ones you specially chose. You beat the living daylights out of the evil king, stripped him bare from head to toe, stuck his own head on his spear, and blew his army away. They were scattered to the four winds—and ended up as shark food! You galloped through the Sea on your horses, riding the top of the waves. When I heard all that, my stomach did a complete flip. I was stammering and couldn't even talk right. My bones felt like jelly. I was stumbling all over the place. Now I'm just sitting back, waiting for the end of the world to come down on the people attacking us.

Even if the cherry trees don't bloom and the strawberries don't get ripe, even if the apples are all nasty with worms and the wheat fields are a total fail, even if there are no sheep in the pens and no cows in the barns, I'm still going to be singing joyful praises to God. I'm doing cartwheels of joy for my Savior God. I'm counting on God's rule to win in the end, so I'm feeling brave and getting stronger. I can run like a deer. I feel like I'm the king of the mountain!
(For the whole church to sing, with a full orchestra.)
